$schema.description: The JSON Schema your editor checks this file against. acorn doesn't read it.

id.description: The plugin's permanent ID: 2 to 32 lowercase letters, digits, and dashes, starting with a letter. It names your routes and your storage, so a new ID is a new plugin.

name.description: The plugin's name, as Settings and the agent tool list show it. The trust prompt shows the `id`.

icon.description: The plugin's logo, registered as `brand:<id>`, so any contribution can name it as its glyph.

d.description: One SVG path's `d` attribute, drawn in a 24 by 24 box. A whole SVG file is refused.

color.description: The brand's color as six-digit hex, such as `#24292f`. Any other CSS color is refused.

icons.description: More brand marks, for a package that shows several brands, at most 16. The key `github` becomes `brand:<id>/github`.

d.description: One SVG path's `d` attribute, drawn in a 24 by 24 box. A whole SVG file is refused.

color.description: The brand's color as six-digit hex, such as `#24292f`. Any other CSS color is refused.

version.description: Your plugin's own version, such as `1.2.0`. Another plugin's `requires` entry compares its range with this version's major.

baseline.description: The acorn baseline this manifest is written for. It must be `acorn-1`.

emits.description: Event verbs your plugin announces, so other plugins can subscribe to them. Your own frames and trees hear your events without this.

verb.description: The event's verb, sent on `plugin:<id>:<verb>`: lowercase, starting with a letter, with no colon.

description.description: What the event means. The plugin's settings page shows it as plain text.

clients.description: The apps your client half runs in: `desktop`, `terminal`, or both. Leave it out to run in every app, because an empty list is refused.

apiVersion.description: The plugin API majors your plugin works with: one major such as `"5"`, a list such as `"4 || 5"`, or a span such as `"4-5"`. A range that leaves out acorn's major doesn't load.

requires.description: What your plugin needs from the rest of the Node before it can work.

plugins.description: Each plugin yours needs. When one is missing or the wrong major, the plugin list says which before anything runs.

id.description: The ID of the plugin yours needs.

version.description: A range over the needed plugin's major, written like `apiVersion`. Leave it out to accept any version.

node.description: Your Node half's entry file, relative to the plugin folder, such as `node/index.js`. Leave it out when the plugin has no Node half.

client.description: Your client bundle, one JavaScript file relative to the plugin folder, which draws your frames and trees.

migrations.description: Your folder of Drizzle migrations, relative to the plugin folder. acorn opens your SQLite file and runs them in order. Never edit one that has shipped.

permissions.description: What your plugin may reach. The person accepts these on each device when they install it.

api.description: acorn API scopes your frames and trees may call through the bridge. Your own routes need none. A scope this acorn doesn't know is denied when you call it, not refused here.

events.description: Event channels your frames and trees may subscribe to: a core channel such as `task.changed`, or another plugin's `plugin:<id>:<verb>` when that plugin declares the verb in `emits`.

node.description: What your Node half may reach. Anything you don't list here is missing from `ctx`.

core.description: Core facets your Node half gets on `ctx.core`, such as `git` or `tasks`. A facet you leave out isn't on `ctx.core`, so your first call to it throws a `TypeError`.

capabilities.description: Other plugins' capabilities your Node half may call, such as `editor.files`. Name the plugin that provides each one in `requires.plugins` too.

secrets.description: Lets your Node half store and read credentials through `ctx.core.secrets`.

exec.description: Lets your Node half run programs through `ctx.core.proc`, the process broker.

net.description: Hosts your Node half may reach with `fetch`, such as `api.linear.app`. A request to any other host fails, and so does a raw socket.

sockets.description: Unrestricted socket access, for a protocol that can't go through `fetch`. It's a broad grant, so ask for `net` instead whenever `fetch` will do.

env.description: Environment variables your Node half inherits from the Node, by name. Without them it gets a base environment that holds no credentials.

files.description: Files outside your plugin's folder that your Node half may open. A path inside acorn's own data folder is refused.

env.description: The environment variable that holds the file's path. The host reads it when your Node half starts, so the manifest never holds one machine's path.

access.description: `read`, or `read-write` to let your Node half replace the file too.

contributions.description: Everything your plugin adds to acorn, by kind. A key this acorn doesn't know is reported and skipped, so a manifest written for a newer acorn still loads.

frames.description: Surfaces your client bundle draws: panes, reference panels, settings pages, importers, overlays, webviews, core replacements, and rectangles for another plugin's point. `target` says which.

target.description: What the surface is: a `pane`, a reference panel, a settings page, a project importer, a `webview`, an `overlay`, a replacement for one of acorn's own surfaces, or an `inline` rectangle for another plugin's point.

scope.description: For a `pane`: whether it belongs to a task, or to a project beside your rail list.

id.description: The surface's ID, unique in this manifest. A pane's ID is stored in people's layouts, so don't rename it.

label.description: The surface's name, in the pane switcher, Settings, or the trust prompt.

glyph.description: A Lucide icon name, or a `brand:` mark.

order.description: Where it sits among its siblings. Lower comes first.

showInSwitcher.description: Set `false` to leave a pane out of the switcher, so only a command opens it.

readsArchived.description: For a task pane that draws only from stored history: show it on archived tasks too.

statusAnnotations.description: For a task pane: let other plugins put status marks on its switcher button, through the `core:pane` point.

availability.description: For a task pane: a GET route that answers `{ [taskId]: boolean }`, so the pane hides on tasks it has nothing for. A task left out is hidden too.

formFactor.description: The screen sizes the surface works at.

providerId.description: For a reference panel or task pane: the integration it shows items from. A task pane with one hides on tasks with no link from that integration.

group.description: For `settings`: `workspace` makes a workspace settings page.

category.description: For `settings`: the Settings group the page sits in. Defaults to Features, and an unknown value is reported and ignored.

settingsScope.description: For `settings`: what a change on the page affects. Defaults to `node`.

keywords.description: Words Settings search matches besides the label.

sections.description: For `settings`: the page's sections, each a search result and a link target. IDs must differ.

id.description: The section's anchor, matching a `SettingsSection` on the page.

label.description: The section's name in search results.

keywords.description: Words Settings search matches besides the label.

railSourceVisibility.description: For `settings`: your own sources that get a **Show in left rail** switch above the page.

coreSlot.description: For `coreSlot`, and required there: which of acorn's surfaces you offer to draw. The person chooses it in Settings, and acorn draws its own again if yours fails.

placesSlots.description: For a `rail` or `topbar` replacement: the nested slot your surface places, so Settings can warn when you leave it out.

url.description: For `webview`: the page it opens. Give `url` or `urlSource`, not both.

urlSource.description: For `webview`: a route on your Node half that answers `{ url }`, when the start page depends on the task.

hosts.description: For `webview`, and required there: the hosts the page may visit, including through redirects. The trust prompt lists them.

layout.description: For a `pane`: the host's arrangement, filled from `regions`. Leave it out for one frame that fills the pane.

regions.description: With `layout`: what fills each of the layout's regions, by region name: `"frame"`, a `remote` tree, or a `document`.

kind.description: A tree your client bundle draws with the host's components.

entry.description: The `mountTree` entry that draws this region.

kind.description: A document the host's editor draws, read and written through your routes.

languageId.description: The document's language, for highlighting, in LSP's spelling such as `typescript`.

read.description: A GET route that answers `{ text }`. The host fills in `:taskId` and `:projectId`, and no other parameter.

write.description: A PUT route sent `{ text }` when the person saves. Leave it out for a read-only document.

route.description: A POST route sent the text and cursor position that answers completion items.

triggerCharacters.description: Characters that open the completion list mid-word, such as `.`.

hover.description: Text shown when the person hovers over the document.

route.description: A POST route on your Node half, sent the live text and its `revision`. Echo the revision in the answer.

diagnostics.description: Errors and warnings drawn in the document.

route.description: A POST route on your Node half, sent the live text and its `revision`. Echo the revision in the answer.

collapsible.description: For a `list-detail` pane: let the person collapse the list.

claimsKeys.description: Shortcuts your frame keeps instead of passing to acorn. Each needs meta, ctrl, or alt, and acorn's own are refused. Your code may claim fewer, never more.

destinations.description: Views in other plugins your tree may ask to open, each named here so the trust prompt shows it.

id.description: The destination's ID, which your tree names when it asks to go there.

label.description: What the trust prompt calls the destination.

targetKind.description: The kind of thing it opens, which the plugin that owns that view presents.

noticeKind.description: The notice kind sent with it, when it isn't the plugin default.

sources.description: Sources on the left rail. The host draws the list from your route, or your tree draws it.

id.description: The source's ID, unique in this manifest.

label.description: The source's name on the rail and in the palette.

glyph.description: A Lucide icon name, or a `brand:` mark, for the rail.

order.description: Where the source sits on the rail. Lower comes first. Required, because load order never decides it.

providerId.description: Shows the source only while this integration is connected.

items.description: A GET route on your Node half that answers the rail's rows. Give `items` or `tree`, not both.

search.description: A GET route that searches the same list, sent the person's `q`. Needs `items`.

tree.description: Two trees from your client bundle that draw the list and its detail, for a source with no Node half. Give `items` or `tree`, not both.

list.description: The `mountTree` entry that draws the list.

detail.description: The `mountTree` entry that draws the selected row's detail.

projectScoped.description: Set it when the list depends on the open project. The rail then shows a project picker and sends `?project=` to `items`.

showInRailByDefault.description: Whether the desktop rail shows the source's icon before the person chooses. Defaults to `true`.

requiresGitProject.description: Shows the source only while the workspace has a project that's a Git repository.

statusAnnotations.description: Lets other plugins put status marks on the source's rail icon, through the `core:source` point.

defaultPane.description: The task pane a task from this source opens on the first time. It must be one of your own task panes.

onSelect.description: What picking a row does. It takes every action verb.

verb.description: Opens one of your task panes in the open task. The clicked row's ID goes with it.

pane.description: The ID of a `pane` this manifest declares under `frames`.

verb.description: Goes to the task the clicked row names. Only a dashboard row names one, and a row that names no task gets a toast saying so.
Goes to one of your project panes for the clicked row, at the address its `routes` entry declares. Needs a selected row and a project.

surface.description: The ID of a `scope: 'project'` pane this manifest declares.

verb.description: POSTs to a route on your Node half. The body says what was clicked, and its shape depends on where the action sits.

path.description: The route to POST, one of your own.

verb.description: Starts a new task from the selected rail row. Only a rail source's `onSelect` takes it.

emptyState.description: What the rail says when `items` answers with no rows. It isn't shown when the route fails.

message.description: What the rail says when your route answers with no items. Plain text.

action.description: One action the empty rail offers, as a button.

views.description: The views a person may pick for a panel here. Leave it out to allow every view.

refresh.description: Seconds between rereads of the route, at least 30. A fallback: push changes with `ctx.events.status()` instead of polling.

slots.description: Badges the host draws in the top bar or in a task's footer, from your route.

id.description: The badge's ID, unique in this manifest.

slot.description: Where the badge goes: `topbar`, after the notification bell, or `footer`, in a task's footer.

icon.description: A Lucide icon name, or a `brand:` mark.

data.description: A GET route that answers the badge, or `null` to hide it.

surface.description: With `when: 'surface'`, the ID of the pane the chord works in.

nodeStats.description: Numbers on a Node's card on Fleet home, read from your route.

order.description: Where the stat sits on the card. Lower comes first.

label.description: The label in singular and plural, such as `["card stuck", "cards stuck"]`, so the card reads "1 card stuck".

data.description: A GET route that answers the number.

contentLinks.description: Links in acorn that open your pane, reference panel, or overlay, matched by URL.

id.description: The link's ID, unique in this manifest.

match.description: The URLs this link claims, such as `https://linear.app/{team}/issue/{id}`: `https`, a literal host, and literal or `{capture}` path parts. Needs `item`.

openPane.description: A task pane in this manifest the link can open.

openOverlay.description: An overlay in this manifest the link can open.

item.description: The `{capture}` in `match` that names the item. Required with `match`.

presentations.description: The ways the link may open. The surface the link is clicked in picks one.

routes.description: App URLs that open one of your project panes on an item.

id.description: The route's ID, unique in this manifest.

path.description: The app address, inside `/p/:projectId/x/<id>/`, with a `:param` for the item, such as `/p/:projectId/x/acme/issue/:issueId`.

surface.description: The `scope: 'project'` pane in this manifest the address opens.

item.description: The `:param` in `path` that holds the item. It can't be `projectId`, which the host binds itself.

order.description: The order the host matches routes in. Put a fixed path before a `:param` path that would also match it.

agentContexts.description: Entries in an agent composer's context list, each a snapshot your routes provide.

id.description: The entry's ID, unique in this manifest.

label.description: The entry's name in the composer's context list.

options.description: A GET route sent `taskId` that answers the options the person can pick.

capture.description: A POST route sent the picked `optionIds` that answers the text to attach. The host stamps the source and time itself.

refResolvers.description: Routes that turn your items' identifiers into labels, for surfaces that show them.

id.description: The resolver's ID, unique in this manifest.

kind.description: The kind of item it labels, such as `issue`.

resolve.description: A POST route sent `{ identifiers }` that answers a label for each. There's no single-item form: send an array of one.

themes.description: Color themes for Settings > Appearance, written as token values. You write no CSS.

id.description: The theme's ID, in lowercase letters, digits, and dashes. The host makes it `plugin:<pluginId>:<id>`.

label.description: The theme's name in Settings > Appearance.

dark.description: Whether the theme is dark. The host sets `--is-dark` and `--color-scheme` from it, so don't set those as tokens.

tokens.description: A color for every palette token, and no others. Each is a hex color or a flat color function, such as `#1e1e2e` or `oklch(0.7 0.15 250)`.

styles.description: Style packs for Settings > Appearance, written as token values the host checks.

id.description: The style pack's ID, in lowercase letters, digits, and dashes.

label.description: The style pack's name in Settings > Appearance.

description.description: One line about how the style pack looks.

tokens.description: Style tokens and their values, such as radius and spacing. The host checks each one and refuses a value it can't use.

contextMenus.description: Rows on acorn's context menus, such as a task row, an Editor file, or selected text.

location.description: Which menu the row goes on.

surface.description: For a rail location, which of your own sources the menu belongs to. Required there, and not used elsewhere.

label.description: The row's text.

icon.description: A Lucide icon name, or a `brand:` mark.

order.description: Where the row sits. acorn's own rows come first unless yours is lower.

when.description: Facts the target must match for the row to show, such as `{ "extension": "md" }`. Every value must equal the target's, with no patterns. A fact the location doesn't have is refused.

verb.description: Opens an address in the person's browser, not inside acorn.

url.description: The address to open. Only `https` opens.

verb.description: Opens one of your overlays over the window.

overlay.description: The ID of an `overlay` this manifest declares under `frames`.

verb.description: Sends the command's ID to a frame or tree region of one of your panes, for a shortcut pressed where your pane has no keyboard, such as in a document region's editor.

surface.description: The ID of a pane this manifest declares.

action.description: What the row does. It gets the ID of what was right-clicked.

extensionPoints.description: Places in your own views that other plugins may fill.

id.description: The point's ID, in lowercase letters, digits, and dashes. Others name it as `<yourPluginId>:<id>`.

label.description: What you're opening, in your words. Both plugins' trust prompts show it.

kind.description: What a contributor brings: `rows` from a route, `annotation` marks, a `remote` tree, a `rectangle` frame, or a `hook` handler.

location.description: Where on your surface the host draws the point. Required for `rows` and `rectangle`, refused for the other kinds.

surface.description: Which of your own panes the point sits on, for `rows` and `rectangle`.

panels.description: For `pane.aside` only: what the person may put in the dashboard region. Leave it out for your own sources, every view, and four panels.

sources.description: The sources a panel here may be built from, as `<pluginId>:<sourceId>`. Leave it out for your own sources. Don't set it with `fieldRole`.

fieldRole.description: Instead of `sources`: any source with a field in this role, including ones installed later.

views.description: The views a person may pick for a panel here. Leave it out to allow every view.

max.description: How many panels fit in the region.

key.description: For `annotation`, and required there: the fields your items are keyed by, and each one's type.

mode.description: For `remote` and `rectangle`: `replace` draws one contributor, and `stack` draws several, up to `max`.

selector.description: For `replace`: what the key you pass names, such as `mime` or `path`, so Settings can say what the person picks between.

max.description: For `stack`: how many contributors draw before the host folds the rest away.

accepts.description: For `remote` and `rectangle`: the key values you'll pass, as a guide for contributors' `matches`. It's advisory.

actions.description: For `remote`: action names a contributor's tree may ask you to run with `mount.host.invoke`. You bind a handler for each in your own tree.

mounts.description: For `remote`: where the host draws the point outside your tree, above or below your views, so you write no `Slot`.

surface.description: One of your project panes or reference panels.

region.description: Above the view, `header`, or below it, `footer`.

payload.description: For `hook`, and required there: the fields a handler receives, and their types.

allows.description: For `hook`: the modes a handler may ask for. A handler asking for another gets nothing.

timeoutMs.description: For `hook`: how long one handler may take, in milliseconds.

onTimeout.description: For `hook`: what a veto handler that runs out of time counts as.

order.description: For `hook`: run handlers by their `priority`, then install time, or by install time alone.

collect.description: For `hook`: run every veto handler instead of stopping at the first, so you can show every reason.

extensions.description: What you add to another plugin's extension point: rows, a tree, a rectangle, marks, or a hook handler.

id.description: The contribution's ID, unique in this manifest.

point.description: The point you fill, as `<ownerPluginId>:<pointId>`. If the owner isn't installed, nothing shows, with no error.

label.description: The heading above your rows, and your contribution's name in Settings. The host shows your plugin's name beside it.

order.description: Where your rows sit among other contributors'. Lower comes first.

items.description: For a `rows` or `annotation` point: a route on your Node half that answers the rows or marks. Name exactly one of `items`, `remote`, `frame`, and `route`.

remote.description: For a `remote` point: the `mountTree` entry in your client bundle that draws your tree.

frame.description: For a `rectangle` point: an `inline` frame in this manifest.

route.description: For a `hook` point: a route on your Node half the host calls with the payload. Needs `mode`.

matches.description: For `remote` and `frame`: the keys you draw for, exactly or as `prefix*` or `*suffix`. Leave it out to draw for every key.

overlay.description: For `remote`: one of your own overlays your tree may ask the host to open.

mode.description: For `route`, and required there: what the handler asks to do: `observe`, `transform`, `veto`, or `ask`.

priority.description: For a hook handler: where it runs in the chain, when the owner orders by priority. Lower runs first.

onSelect.description: For `items` rows: what picking a row does. It gets the row's ID.

verb.description: Opens one of your task panes in the open task. The clicked row's ID goes with it.

pane.description: The ID of a `pane` this manifest declares under `frames`.

verb.description: Goes to the task the clicked row names. Only a dashboard row names one, and a row that names no task gets a toast saying so.
POSTs to a route on your Node half. The body says what was clicked, and its shape depends on where the action sits.

path.description: The route to POST, one of your own.

verb.description: Opens an address in the person's browser, not inside acorn.

url.description: The address to open. Only `https` opens.

verb.description: Opens one of your overlays over the window.

overlay.description: The ID of an `overlay` this manifest declares under `frames`.

verb.description: Sends the command's ID to a frame or tree region of one of your panes, for a shortcut pressed where your pane has no keyboard, such as in a document region's editor.

surface.description: The ID of a pane this manifest declares.

refresh.description: Seconds between rereads of the route, at least 30. A fallback: push changes with `ctx.events.status()` instead of polling.

documentServices.description: Hover and diagnostics for Editor's files in one language, from your routes.

id.description: The service's ID, unique in this manifest.

label.description: The service's name, shown when two plugins serve one language and the person picks.

languageId.description: The language of the Editor files it serves, in LSP's spelling such as `python`.

hover.description: Text shown when the person hovers in a file. Give `hover`, `diagnostics`, or both.

route.description: A POST route on your Node half, sent the live text and its `revision`. Echo the revision in the answer.

diagnostics.description: Errors and warnings drawn in a file. Read only: no fixes.

route.description: A POST route on your Node half, sent the live text and its `revision`. Echo the revision in the answer.

dataSources.description: Typed data sources your Node half serves, for dashboards and workflows.

sourceId.description: The source's ID, unique in this manifest. Others name it as `<pluginId>:<sourceId>`.

name.description: The source's name, such as `Release readiness`.

singular.description: What one record is called, such as `Issue`.

plural.description: What several are called, such as `Issues`.

identityScope.description: A sentence saying what a record's ID is and what keeps it stable, such as `GitHub GraphQL node ID; stable across renames`.

icon.description: A Lucide icon name, or a `brand:` mark.

providerId.description: The integration whose connection each query picks. Not with `inputs`.

titlePointer.description: A pointer to the field that titles a record.

urlPointer.description: A pointer to the field that holds a record's web address.

handler.description: The route on your Node half that answers the source's operations.

source.description: The source this input reads, as `<pluginId>:<sourceId>`. It must be registered statically, not discovered.

label.description: The input's name where the person picks an account for it.

optional.description: Whether the person may skip it. A skipped input is `undefined` in your query.

inputs.description: For a derived source: other sources the host reads for you, by input name, at most eight. The person approves them before your plugin reads anything.

dataSourceDiscoveries.description: Routes that list data sources your plugin can offer, found when someone asks.

discoveryId.description: The discovery's ID, unique in this manifest.

handler.description: The route on your Node half that lists sources, at most 100 a page. A discovered source is available only in the scope that found it.

providerId.description: The integration whose connection each discovery uses.

schedules.description: Work the Node runs for your plugin on a cadence, with no client open.

id.description: The schedule's ID, unique in this manifest.

name.description: The schedule's name in Settings > Schedules and the trust prompt.

run.description: A POST route on your Node half the Node calls each time, sent `{ scheduleId }`. Only success or failure is read from the answer.

every.description: Seconds between runs, at most a week.

daily.description: A time each day, as `HH:MM` in the Node's local time.

day.description: The day of the week, 0 to 6, where 0 is Sunday.

at.description: The time, as `HH:MM` in the Node's local time.

weekly.description: A day and time each week.

cadence.description: How often it runs: every so many seconds, daily, or weekly. A plugin's schedule runs at most every 300 seconds, whatever it asks.

timeout.description: How long one run may take, in seconds, not milliseconds. Defaults to 60.

taskChecks.description: Checks the host runs before it archives a task, each with an optional cleanup.

id.description: The check's ID, unique in this manifest.

check.description: A GET route sent `taskId` that answers `{ concern }`, or `{ concern: null }` when there's nothing to say. Keep that answer cheap.

apply.description: A POST route that does the cleanup the concern offered, run only if the person leaves its box ticked. Leave it out for a warning with no cleanup.

timeout.description: Seconds. Parsed but not used: every check runs under the Node's own short limit, because the person is waiting.

auditActions.description: Verbs your Node half may write to the audit log with `ctx.audit.record`. An undeclared verb is refused.

id.description: The verb, in lowercase letters, digits, dots, and dashes, such as `run.finished`. No colon: the host makes it `<pluginId>:<id>`.

label.description: What the audit log calls the action.

harnesses.description: Agent programs acorn can run as managed sessions. You declare the program, and acorn runs it.

id.description: The harness's ID. The host makes it `<pluginId>:<id>` and stores it on every session, so renaming it breaks existing sessions.

label.description: The harness's name where a person picks an agent.

glyph.description: A Lucide icon name, or a `brand:` mark. `brand:<pluginId>` is your manifest's `icon`.

command.description: A program found on the `PATH`, such as `opencode`. Name `command` or `entry`, not both.

entry.description: A JavaScript file in your package that acorn runs with the Node's own runtime, for an adapter in front of an agent that doesn't speak ACP.

requires.description: With `entry`: the agent program your adapter drives.

command.description: The agent's program, looked up on the `PATH`.

env.description: The variable that carries the program's full path to your adapter.

spawn.description: How acorn starts the agent for a managed session. It speaks ACP.

envPassthrough.description: Environment variables passed from the Node to the agent, by name or as a `PREFIX_*` glob. A bare `*` is refused, and the trust prompt lists them.

quirks.description: What the agent supports that ACP doesn't say.

manualCompaction.description: The agent has a compact command, so the Agent pane offers Compact.

sessionPersistence.description: Sessions outlive the agent's process and can be loaded again, so resume works.

probes.description: Routes on your Node half the Agent pane asks about the agent's account. Without them it shows less.

usage.description: A route that answers the account's plan usage, for the Agent pane.

auth.description: A route that answers whether the agent's account is signed in.

terminal.description: The agent's interactive program, offered in a task terminal. Leave it out for an agent with no interactive mode.

oneShot.description: One prompt in, one answer out, with no session. It puts the harness in every Generate list.

command.description: The program, when the harness has no `terminal` to take it from. Refused beside a `terminal`.

args.description: The arguments that make the program answer once and exit, such as `["run"]`. The prompt goes last.

modelFlag.description: The flag that picks a model, such as `--model`. Leave it out and a model a caller names is dropped.

output.description: How to read the answer: `text` takes all of standard output, and `json-lines` looks for a `result` event in a stream of JSON lines.

customAgents.description: Saved agents a person can start: a harness, its options, and instructions.

id.description: The agent's ID, in lowercase letters, digits, and dashes. The host makes it `<pluginId>:<id>`.

name.description: The name the person picks the agent by.

glyph.description: A Lucide icon name, or a `brand:` mark.

description.description: One line about what the agent is for.

harness.description: The harness it runs on: `claude`, `codex`, another plugin's `<pluginId>:<harnessId>`, or the ID of a harness this manifest declares.

options.description: Provider options to start with, by option ID. An option the harness doesn't offer is dropped when the session starts, with a line in the transcript.

instructions.description: Text for the agent's system prompt. The trust prompt shows it in full, and a version that changes it asks the person again.

maxToolRisk.description: The riskiest of acorn's own tools the agent may call: `read`, `write`, or `execute`.

skills.description: Folders holding a `SKILL.md` that every managed agent session can load by name.

id.description: The skill's name, in lowercase letters, digits, and dashes. Agents see it as `<pluginId>:<id>`.

path.description: The skill's folder in your package. It holds a `SKILL.md` and anything it uses.

agentTools.description: Tools agents can call, each answered by a route on your Node half.

id.description: The tool's ID, in lowercase snake case starting with a letter. Agents see it as `<pluginId>_<id>`.

description.description: What the tool does and when to call it. Agents read this to choose it, and the trust prompt shows it.

inputSchema.description: A JSON Schema for the tool's arguments, of type `object`. Only a small set of keywords is accepted, within size and depth limits.

risk.description: How much the tool can change. The person's tool tiers decide whether agents may call it.

scope.description: Always `task`: the tool runs for one task's agents.

handler.description: A POST route on your Node half the host calls with the arguments. The host sends the verified task and session, and never retries.

requiresSession.description: Hide the tool from a caller without a signed task and session, such as a terminal session.

timeoutMs.description: How long a call may take, in milliseconds.

maxOutputBytes.description: The largest answer the host accepts, in bytes.

contextSections.description: Sections of a task's context, each read from a route on your Node half.

id.description: The section's ID, in lowercase snake case starting with a letter.

label.description: The section's name in the task's context list.

scope.description: Always `task`: the section is part of one task's context.

order.description: Where the section sits in the context. Lower comes first.

read.description: A route on your Node half that answers `{ items, compact, unavailable? }`: reference data and short text, never markup.

defaultIncluded.description: Whether a task includes the section before the person chooses.

timeoutMs.description: How long the read may take, in milliseconds.

maxBytes.description: The most bytes the section may add.

maxTokens.description: The most tokens the section may add.

cliCommands.description: Commands under `acorn plugin`, each answered by a `/cli/<name>` route on your Node half.

name.description: The command's name after `acorn plugin <pluginId>`, in lowercase kebab case.

summary.description: One or two sentences of help.

effects.description: What the command changes. Required when `risk` is `write`.

risk.description: Whether the command only reads, or changes something.

scope.description: What the command acts on. `inputSchema` must require `nodeId`, and the ID this scope names, as strings.

capability.description: The core facet the command needs, such as `projects:read`. Declare it in `permissions.node.core` too: this field grants nothing.

inputSchema.description: A JSON Schema for the command's input, of type `object`, in the same language as an agent tool's.

outputSchema.description: A JSON Schema for your route's answer, of type `object`.

route.description: The route on your Node half that runs the command.

browserHandoffs.description: Buttons the browser extension draws on a website, which hand the page's item to a task.

id.description: The handoff's ID, in lowercase letters, digits, and dashes.

label.description: The button's text, drawn as plain text.

glyph.description: A Lucide icon name for the sidebar's item card.

match.description: The pages the button appears on, such as `https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/pull/{number}`: `https`, a literal host, and literal or `{capture}` path parts.

anchors.description: CSS selectors tried in order. The button goes at the end of the first element found. When none match, the sidebar still offers the handoff.

resolve.description: A POST route on your Node half, sent `{ url, captures }`, that answers the page's items.

taskAddresses.description: A GET route on your Node half listing the local origins your tasks' apps answer at, for the browser extension.

browserPanel.description: A read-only panel in the browser extension's sidebar for a task, served by a route on your Node half. One per plugin.

label.description: The panel's name in the sidebar's navigation.

glyph.description: A Lucide icon name for the navigation item.

pane.description: A task pane in this manifest that **Open in Acorn** opens.

route.description: A GET route sent `taskId` that answers the panel's blocks, or 404 for a task with no panel.

codeHost.description: The Git hosts whose repositories your plugin names, and how acorn treats their change requests.

label.description: The host's name as a person reads it, such as `GitLab`.

hosts.description: Bare lowercase host names, such as `gitlab.com`, with no scheme or port.

changeRequest.description: How acorn treats this host's pull or merge requests. Every field is optional.

ref.description: The ref acorn fetches to check one out, holding `{number}` once, such as `merge-requests/{number}/head`. Without it, acorn fetches the source branch.

label.description: What a person calls one in an error, such as `merge request`. Defaults to `change request`.

prefix.description: The mark before its number in a task title, such as `!`. Defaults to `#`.

pane.description: The pane that shows one. A task whose main change request is on this host opens on it.
